content.introduction: According to BlackRock, 89% of healthcare companies within the S&P 500 exceeded earnings expectations in the four quarters of 2025, ranking second among all sectors. Analysts anticipate an acceleration in healthcare earnings growth in 2027, driven by pharmaceuticals and managed care. The sector’s innovative edge comes with relatively low correlation to tech and the broader tech-driven U.S. stock market, and with historical elements of resilience, making tech and healthcare powerful portfolio complements.
body:
Fundamentals are strong. 89% of healthcare companies within the S&P 500 exceeded earnings expectations in the four quarters of 2025, ranking second among all sectors.3 In addition to broadly exceeding earnings expectations over recent quarters, analysts anticipate an acceleration in healthcare earnings growth in 2027, driven by pharmaceuticals and managed care.4 [...] Today, as investors are starting to look for areas of opportunity outside of technology, we believe some capital could find its way back to healthcare. The sector’s innovative edge comes with relatively low correlation to tech ― and the broader tech-driven U.S. stock market ― and with historical elements of resilience. This could make tech and healthcare powerful portfolio complements.

BlackRock's iShares is trying to appeal to investors who want to diversify beyond from the so-called Magnificent Seven.

The firm launched the iShares Top 20 U.S. Stocks ETF (TOPT) this month. It doesn't just hold the Magnificent Seven — Apple, Amazon, Meta, Alphabet, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla. It's made up of the 20 largest U.S. stocks by market capitalization. [...] Aguirre, the firm's head of U.S. iShares product, noted the ETF's mission is to deliver an easy and accessible way to tap into the innovation of megacaps – "whether that be in the tech-heavy Nasdaq space or, more broadly, within the S&P ."

The ETF, according to Aguirre, provides a way for investors worried about the concentration of the Magnificent Seven stocks in the S&P 500.
